bluf: LaFleur Marketing is a founder led Grand Rapids, MI agency founded 2015 selling data insights, storytelling and design to law firms through a registered CLEAR framework, with Clearboard, an AI dashboard tying marketing to signed clients, as its newest product. The record shows an AI forward small shop, with AI consulting, an llms.txt and a 2023 Inc. 5000 listing, that sells paid search and runs no Google ads of its own. The one thing a rival should know: the Horus read is Favored at 19.1, but the Monsoon displacement of 66.0 on an SMB legal book means it is likely undercut on price by an offshore delivered rival.
doing:
LaFleur Marketing positions itself as a Grand Rapids full service agency for law firms and regulated professional services, blending data insights, storytelling and design through its CLEAR framework: in plain words, a small legal marketing shop selling a named method and a dashboard rather than hours. Its headline claim is the 2023 Inc. 5000 listing and results such as a 126% conversion increase, with an Addy award winning project on the homepage.

The mix is twelve services, from SEO, local and AI search, paid advertising, website design and content strategy through social, automation and analytics to AI consulting, AI dashboards, fractional marketing and hosting. Two lines lead at 3: Content & Digital PR (storytelling headlines the title and H1, with a content strategy page built on a Crosley Law example) and Data & Measurement (data insights lead the H1 and Clearboard links marketing to signed clients). Four core lines score 2: AI Automation / Agents on a dedicated human centered AI consulting and AI audit page; Paid Search on a paid advertising page covering PPC and LSAs with Michigan Auto Law test and learn campaigns; SEO on a services section pairing SEO with local and AI search; and Web & Product on WordPress, Shopify, HubSpot and headless builds. Two proprietary assets are listed, the registered CLEAR framework and Clearboard; no partner is listed.

Its AI posture is direct: it sells human centered AI consulting and adoption audits, and Clearboard answers plain language questions about traffic and signed clients.

Moves in date order: 2020, recognised among Best and Brightest Companies to Work For; 2023, named to the Inc. 5000; 2025, the Clearboard launch announced, undated, with the news index last updated in March 2025. Pricing signals stop at a lightweight, budget friendly site tier for newer firms with no prices shown. Absent: no jobs, no partner badge, no case study beyond three service page examples, and no news since 2025.
clients:
The record marks its client type as SMB and lists five verticals: legal, financial services, healthcare, technology and professional services, and it is filed under legal. The home market is the US, with Grand Rapids, MI the only office listed.

The book holds 3 clients and all 3 carry an observed need, a small but fully described book: Michigan Auto Law came for paid performance, cited on the paid advertising services page for test and learn campaigns; Crosley Law came for PR, reputation and content, cited as the example on the content strategy services page; and Global Impact came for brand and creative plus web build and platform, cited on the website design services page. The signals are service page examples rather than standalone case studies, so the evidence is observed but thin, and the 126% conversion increase on the homepage is not tied to a named client in the record.

No client on record sits on another tracked agency's book.

The tailwinds are KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation), driven by AI Search / GEO and Content & Digital PR, and KJ4 (the platforms absorbing execution), where Data & Measurement outweighs the paid lines, so it is likely, with moderate confidence, that law firm clients ask for AI search visibility and for measurement tying spend to signed clients next, which Clearboard already names. The exposure is KJ5 (the price of attention splits in two) on Paid Social and Programmatic & CTV, both scoring 1, so it is a roughly even chance that the paid social hours in its mix are the first a firm cuts.
house: The record marks 1 of 2 say and do lines practised and house integrity at 50. Paid Search is contradicted, the one gap listed: it sells paid search and runs no Google ads of its own in the Transparency Center, where its record shows 0 ads. Publishing cadence is corroborated by 6 sitemap URLs updated in 90 days and 64 in 365 out of 312. It publishes an llms.txt, blocks no AI crawlers, and 4 AI URLs were found. The tag stack is gtm, ga4 and hubspot on WordPress, with no social pixel, test tool or ABM stack. LinkedIn's ad library returned not found: 98 ads match the name query, the near name advertiser LaFleur Minerals Inc (20) was excluded, and 0 company ads remain. No Meta or TikTok check is recorded. The social links are LinkedIn, Instagram and Facebook.
market:
The Horus read puts LaFleur Marketing at a tailwind index of 19.1, band Favored. It is best placed for KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) at net 0.199, driven by AI Search / GEO and Content & Digital PR, and for KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer) at 0.159, where Data & Measurement outweighs the paid lines; it is most exposed to KJ5 (the price of attention splits in two) at -0.061, a shallow headwind. The best scenario fit is The Walled Oasis at 36/100. It is making P3 (LSAs and Sponsored Places) and P4 (inputs for automation); P1, P6 and P7 are partial; P2 and P8 are absent; P5 unknown.

The Monsoon read is 60.0, band Onshore wind, migration 54.0 against displacement 66.0, inferred from the SMB ICP term. 54 of the index is the sold mix, SEO (8) and Web & Product (8) most movable; the shore split sends 65% to South and Southeast Asia and 25% to Latin America. No hub office or onshore claim is listed.
openings:
The strongest opening is price. Displacement 66.0 on the Monsoon read and an SMB legal book make it likely, with moderate confidence (an inferred read), that an offshore delivered rival can undercut its SEO and website hours, above all the lightweight site tier it offers newer firms. The falsifier is a captured pricing page showing outcome priced tiers built on Clearboard's signed client measurement.

The contradiction to lead with is paid search: it sells PPC and LSAs to law firms while its own Transparency Center record shows 0 Google ads, so a rival with live ads of its own can make the say and do point to Michigan Auto Law's peers. P8 is absent, so the first legal agency with results from ads inside AI assistants sets the price.

The gaps are P2, no feed, schema or entity work on its SEO and web lines; P1 partial, AI search sold with no audited citation product despite the dashboard, so an audited number likely wins that conversation; and P5 unknown, so a transparent outcome priced offer is a conversation it cannot have in public. With 3 clients on record, the contest is for the next firm, not the current book.
